subject: Moving BrightLayer from monthly invoicing to annual prepay — proposed structure and ramp
messages:
From: Susan Park <susan.park@brightlayer.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightlayer.com
Date: Sun, 08 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Billing cadence change — moving to annual prepay

Hi Evelyn,

Following our renewal planning session, procurement asked me to see what it would take to move BrightLayer from monthly invoicing to an annual prepay structure for next year. Our objectives are:

- Simplify finance operations (one invoice / year)
- Lock in predictable unit pricing for FY27
- Get a modest term discount in exchange for the prepay

We currently spend ~$120k/month on usage (mostly generation tokens + embeddings). A few specific asks from our CFO:

1) A clear discount schedule for 1yr prepay vs 2yr prepay (and whether pricing is applied to committed $ or expected run-rate).
2) A ramp allowance (we expect 30–50% growth over the year); any true-up or staged credit options?
3) Contractual language for refund/true-up if usage is materially underrun.

Can you share a model (numbers + payment timing) and any standard guardrails you recommend? I attached the redlined SOW we circulated internally.

Thanks — happy to set a time next week to walk through.

Best,
Susan
Procurement Lead, BrightLayer Inc.
[Attachment: BrightLayer_SOW_v2.pdf]
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Susan Park <susan.park@brightlayer.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Billing cadence change — moving to annual prepay

Thanks Susan — great to hear BrightLayer is considering an annual commit. High level response and an initial proposal below.

Quick summary (proposal):
- Year 1 commit: $1,350,000 prepay (equivalent to 11.25 months of current run-rate)
- Discount: 18% term discount applied to list unit rates for the committed volume (applies to tokens and embeddings on committed units)
- Ramp protection: staged true-up credits at 3 milestone checkpoints (month 4, month 8, month 12) if usage growth exceeds committed forecasts; credits are applied against next invoice or refunded at renewal.
- Underrun protection: refundable credit up to 10% of committed spend at year-end if BrightLayer uses <90% of committed units; any refund processed within 60 days after year-end once usage is reconciled.

Attached is a simple price_grid.xlsx that shows per-unit math for 1yr vs 2yr and an example revenue schedule for the numbers you shared.

Operational notes:
- We recommend pinning a model version for mission-critical routes to avoid quality regressions as you scale.
- Billing will be invoiced at time of signing for the full prepay amount; bookkeeping can support an installment schedule (2x or 4x) if you require it — that would reduce the discount to 16% if split over multiple invoices.

Next steps:
1) I can share a surfaced SOW with the exact billing clause changes (refunds/true-ups) — I copied Laura (sales ops) to prepare redlines.
2) Rishi (finance) will confirm the refund mechanics from our end.
3) If the numbers look close, we can book a 30-minute call Wednesday or Thursday next week to finalize.

-Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Enterprise Accounts — Redwood Inference
[evelyn.hart@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123]
[Attachment: price_grid.xlsx]
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Billing cadence change — proposal commentary

Evelyn / Rishi — forwarding Susan's ask and Evelyn's draft proposal. A couple of internal constraints and recommendations before we send formal redlines: 

- Finance likes the staged true-up checkpoints. To be conservative, make the checkpoints tied to cumulative usage vs monthly windows (reduces reconciliation churn).
- Refund window: 60 days is doable but require a clause that refunds are processed net of any overage invoices already billed to avoid disputes.
- Installment option: if BrightLayer wants 2x invoice, reduce term discount by ~200 bps; 4x invoice reduce by ~400 bps. Call these out explicitly in the SOW.
- Approval: anything > $1.2M prepay with refundable credits requires Revenue Ops sign-off (that's on Rishi).

Suggested language snippets to include in redline: "+10% underrun refundable up to X; credits applied at next billing; cumulative milestone measurement; installment discount adjustments" — I'll draft the exact clauses.

-L
Laura Bennett
Senior Sales Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
From: rishi.malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Billing cadence change — proposal commentary

Looping back — I reviewed the numbers and parity with our pricing bands. Approve moving forward with Evelyn's proposal with two adjustments: 

1) Cap refundable underrun at $135,000 (10% of proposed commit) and require BrightLayer to accept the standard audit right to validate usage before refund.
2) Add a clause that if BrightLayer exceeds committed usage by >60% in any 3-month rolling window, we reserve the right to move those routes to on-demand pricing until the next milestone reconciliation.

Once Laura drops the redline with those clauses included, Evelyn — please send to Susan with the price_grid and an optional 2x installment schedule (16% discount) so procurement can choose.

- Rishi
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
